title: eforecast execution, backlog and recovery
description: A16-06. Every value panel sits beside the source gauge that says whether the value means anything. A blank panel is not a quiet system: check the top row.

links.title: What to do about each alert

panels.title: Source availability
panels.description: 0 means we could not read that source. Every panel fed by it is then blank, not zero. This row exists so nobody reads a blank graph as calm. A source this installation does not use (a broker, a cluster) is left out.

panels.title: Oldest unpublished dispatch
panels.description: How long eligible work has waited to reach a worker. Alerts above ten minutes. Blank means the outbox could not be read.

panels.title: Deliveries held open
panels.description: A short dispatcher claims and acknowledges in milliseconds, so this should be zero. Anything else means a consumer is working inside an acknowledgement.

panels.title: Dispatch records by state
panels.description: pending, published, claimed, failed. Four series, whatever the installation does: run and attempt identifiers are never labels.

panels.title: Queue depth by route
panels.description: Our view of the broker. RabbitMQ's own plugin is scraped separately; when the two disagree, that disagreement is the finding.

panels.title: Failed dispatches by classification
panels.description: malformed, unsupported, unroutable, obsolete, exhausted. Each one needs a different action; that is why they are separate rather than a single failure count.

panels.title: Runs waiting, by what for
panels.description: The same words the web UI shows a maintainer: dispatch, worker, image, staging, admission, gpu, cpu, disk, store.

panels.title: Cleanup owed
panels.description: Attempts that owe cleanup. While this is above zero the host's budget is smaller than it looks, and admission will eventually refuse work that should fit.

panels.title: Verified completions
panels.description: Completions accepted with a verified receipt, from the durable counter (eforecast/config/verified_completions.py). A Job exiting 0 is not one of these. Today one venue produces it: an accepted forecast publication, runtime=online.

panels.title: Deliveries that were not dispatches
panels.description: Counted by digest of their own bytes, not accumulated. Usually a version mismatch between publisher and consumer.

panels.title: Tracing one failure to its run

options.content:
These panels deliberately carry **no run, task, attempt or dispatch identifier**: a label per run would make Prometheus grow for every successful job. To go from a number here to the work behind it:

1. **Which attempts?** `bin/eforecast runs --waiting` lists them with their wait reason, or open the Runs panel in the web UI.
2. **Why this one?** `bin/eforecast doctor` names the attempt, its executor and whether that executor is still alive.
3. **What did it say?** The attempt's own log and its durable record in the run store. For a Kubernetes attempt: `kubectl -n eforecast logs -l eforecast.io/attempt=<attempt>`.

The run store is authoritative. A green panel is not evidence that a run succeeded, and this dashboard never claims to be.
